eval only. Evaluation Benchmarks: MedMCQA (MCQ), MedQA (MCQ), MMLU (MCQ, 6 medical subsets), PubMedQA (QA, pqa_labeled subset). SFT Model: MedMCQA 30.5%, MedQA 25.5%, Med MMLU 28.5%, PubMedQA 36%, average 30.125%.

specialty.quote: adapting LLM to medical domain by fine-tuning it (SFT) on medical dataset

serving.notes: generation_config.json sets temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, do_sample true, and max_length 131072. The notebook inference example sets max_new_tokens to 4096. Training used max_seq_length 4096, per_device_train_batch_size 2, gradient_accumulation_steps 4, lora_dropout 0.05, and use_rslora True. The notebook calls merge_and_unload and push_to_hub with this repository id. The tokenizer chat template leaves system_prompt empty. The training string and the multiple-choice prompt are notebook templates, not a stored system prompt. README reports standalone SFT eval loss 1.67.

evaluation_reported.text: On 200-sample subsets, the README's SFT Model row is MedMCQA 30.5%, MedQA 25.5%, Med MMLU 28.5%, PubMedQA 36%, average 30.125%. It says SFT improved MedQA slightly and lowered the average versus the base model. Standalone SFT final evaluation loss is given as 1.67.

discrepancies: Inventory method sft and dataset FreedomIntelligence/medical-o1-reasoning-SFT match the notebook, which uses the English config slice train[:20000]. Inventory parent matches the card (unsloth/deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-1.5b) aside from case. The notebook loads deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and trains with QLoRA, then merges. The card does not state SFT, the dataset, or QLoRA.
